To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SKA‐31, a KCa3.3 and KCa2‐3 activator, improves endothelium‐mediated relaxations in KCa3−/− and NO‐synthase‐deficient mice.
SKA‐31, but not SKA‐20 or SKA‐31 analogues, improved EDHF‐type and NO‐type vasodilation in mice.

SKA‐31, a potent activator of small‐conductance (KCa3.1) and intermediate‐conductances (KCa2.3) Ca2+‐dependent K+‐channels, improved EDHF‐ and nitric oxide‐dependent vasodilation in mice lacking KCa3.2 and NOS3, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the KCa2.2 activator SKA31 and its derivative, the KCa2/KCa3.1 activator SKA20, improve endothelial dysfunction.
the effects of SKA‐31 (SKA‐31) and SKA‐31‐derived compound SKA‐20 (SKA‐20) in isolated mouse arteries.
the role of KCa3/3.1‐type K+ channels in EDHF‐type endothelium‐mediated vasodilations and the effect of the KCa3/2/2.3‐type K+ channel activator SKA on EDHF‐mediated vasocellular responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SKA‐31 is a selective activator of KCa3‐ and KCa2‐channels, but not of KCa1‐channels, that is able to enhance endothelial Ca2+‐signaling and endothelium‐mediated vasodilations.
KCa3.3 channels may play an important role in the endothelium‐mediated vasodilations, but the role of KCa2.1 channels remains controversial.
the results obtained in this study do not support an important role of KCa3 channels in the regulation of EDHF‐type responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SKA‐31‐ and SKA‐31 derivative SKA‐ 20‐induced endothelium‐mediated vasodilations in the mesenteric artery are dependent on the presence of KCa3 and NOS3 channels.
SKA‐31, but not SKA‐20 improved endothelial dysfunction.
SKA‐31, SKA‐20 and SKA‐31/20 are activators of KCa3‐1 and KCa3‐2 channels and improve endothelial dysfunction by activating these two channels in the vascular wall.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SKA‐31, a KCa3.2/KCa2.1/KCa3.1/KKa2.3 activators, and SKA‐30, a KCa2.1/KKa3.1/KC2.3 activater, improve endothelium‐mediated vasodilation and reduce the development of hypertension in KCa3−/− and NO3−/− mouse models.
the SKA‐31 compound is an effective activator of KCa3/KCa2.2 channels in the endothelium.
SKA‐31, SKA‐20 and NS309 are activators of the intermediate‐conductance K+ channel (KCa3.1), and not of the small‐conductance K + channel (KCa2.3).
